elevated.note: Distinct from paper only in dark mode — the plane dialogs, popovers and the command palette sit on.

ink.note: Inverts between themes — never build a fixed-colour scrim or brand chip from this token.

quiet.note: Dark value fixed at #8B8B8B, measured 5.21-5.54:1 against --surface/--elevated (clears 4.5:1 AA). Do not regress to a lower-contrast gray.

scrim.note: Dedicated non-inverting overlay token — exists because ink flips in dark mode.

monument.purpose: The rare page-level statement — a KPI hero number. Most pages never reach for it; it is not a giant uppercase word.

title.purpose: Page heads and dialog titles. Sentence case.

data.purpose: Table cells, fact values, toast messages. Tabular numerals.

prose.purpose: The explanatory line under a heading; dialog descriptions. Capped at 68ch.

legend.purpose: Normal-case labels: section headings, column headers, nav, field labels, filter chips, command-palette results. Never letter-spaced caps.

micro.purpose: Field hints, errors, pagination summaries, status-pill text, kbd hints.

display-customer.purpose: Manrope headings in the obsidian customer world only.

body-customer.purpose: Inter body copy in the obsidian customer world only.

shadows.name: storm-xs
shadows.purpose: Default resting lift for buttons, inputs, KPI cards, mobile roster cards.

shadows.name: storm-sm
shadows.purpose: A surface that needs to read slightly more separate than the default card.

shadows.name: storm-lg
shadows.purpose: Dialog panel, command palette, popovers (notifications/account menu), mobile navigation drawer — the deepest lift.

shadows.name: glow-cyan
shadows.purpose: Customer world only: primary CTAs and focused accent elements on obsidian.

shadows.name: glow-violet
shadows.purpose: Customer world only: secondary accent moments.

shadows.name: panel
shadows.purpose: Customer world only: frosted-glass panels and dropdowns.

motion.name: storm-ring-sweep
motion.purpose: The KPI ring's stroke sweeps in on mount or a real value change. Disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: storm-status-crossfade
motion.value: storm-swap-out 130ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,1,1) both, then storm-swap-in 220ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) both
motion.purpose: A status pill cross-fades colour+label only on a real state change, never on mount. Disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: storm-skeleton-shimmer
motion.purpose: Admin loading skeletons: a soft gradient sweep across paper-lift/mist. Falls back to a flat fill under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: storm-page-in

motion.name: storm-scrim-in

motion.name: storm-rail-width

narrative.northStar: Framer Product Console (admin) over The Obsidian Room (customer)
narrative.overview: This project ships two distinct visual worlds, and they are not variants of each other. They share a Tailwind config and nothing else. The customer-facing world is a premium dark room, unchanged and out of scope for both admin passes. The admin world, "Framer Product Console," replaced the prior "Alphabet Storm" ink-ledger system outright in an earlier pass; this second, EXTEND/HARDEN pass took that white-ground console and hardened it into a modern, premium, production-grade SaaS dashboard (Linear/Vercel/Stripe/Raycast register): first-class light/dark theming via CSS custom properties (not per-component dark: variants), a command palette, a notifications popover, a collapsible sidebar, bulk row selection with client-side CSV export, sticky table headers, and a small disclosed animation system, all layered on the existing one-accent-blue, soft-fill-status, rounded-and-shadowed system without discarding it.
keyCharacteristics: Two scoped worlds; .storm (rooted at #storm-root) is the hard boundary and nothing crosses it.

Admin light: white ground (#FFFFFF) with soft-gray surfaces (#F7F8FA), ink text (#101828), one accent blue (#2563EB), one family (Inter). Admin dark: measured, non-inverted hierarchy (#0A0A0A ground, #111111 surface, #181818 elevated), lifted status hues, translucent-white hairlines.
Status is carried by colour again, as small soft-fill pills with a leading dot — four families (attention / flight / settled / spent) — identical in both themes.
Every surface — card, button, dialog, toast, popover — carries a soft, multi-layer wash shadow; nothing in this world sits flat.
Corners are consistently rounded (rounded-md controls, rounded-xl cards/dialogs/popovers); there is no zero-radius override anywhere in .storm.

A small, disclosed animation system (page transitions, overlay entrances, checkbox check-in, sidebar width) governed by one hard rule: strip fill-mode animation classes on completion for persistent wrapper elements, or fixed-position descendants silently break.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: accent is the only colour in the admin world with no status meaning. It marks "you can act here" — buttons, links, active nav, focus, the command palette's highlighted row. It never appears as a KPI number, a status pill, or a decorative fill.

rules.name: The Soft-Fill Status Rule
rules.body: Status returns to colour in this world: attention/flight/settled/spent each get a fixed hue pair, applied identically everywhere a status appears — pills, badges, KPI numbers, toasts, in both themes. A status rendered only in grey, or in a colour outside its assigned family, is a bug.

rules.name: The Always-Elevated Rule
rules.body: Every rounded surface in .storm carries a soft washed shadow. Nothing in this world sits flat.

rules.name: The Ink-Inverts Rule
rules.body: ink flips between near-black (light) and near-white (dark). Overlays must use the dedicated scrim token, not ink; fixed-colour brand chips must use accent, not ink. Fixed twice this pass: the dialog/palette/drawer scrim, and the login wordmark badge.

rules.name: The Measured Minimum-Contrast Rule
rules.body: quiet's dark value is fixed at #8B8B8B, empirically measured to clear 4.5:1 AA against both --surface and --elevated. Do not regress it to a lower-contrast gray for a quieter look.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Inter carries the entire admin surface, body through label, in both themes. A second family in .storm is a defect.

rules.name: The Normal-Case Rule
rules.body: No admin type role uses uppercase or heavy letter-spacing, except the pre-existing sidebar nav-group label (a structural section marker for a group of links, not a content kicker). Do not extend that exception to new contexts.

rules.name: The No-Absent-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Every card-, button-, dialog- or popover-shaped surface in .storm carries a shadow token; disabled controls are the one exception (shadow-none).

rules.name: The Sticky-Header Placement Rule
rules.body: Sticky positioning and borders on a table header go on individual th elements, not thead — border-collapse makes thead-level sticky/borders unreliable cross-browser.

rules.name: The Strip-The-Fill-Mode-Class Rule
rules.body: Any one-shot entrance animation using animation-fill-mode both/forwards on a persistent, keyed wrapper element must strip its animation class on completion (onAnimationEnd or equivalent), or the resolved transform left behind silently becomes a containing block for position:fixed descendants, breaking every non-portaled dialog/popover inside it. AdminShell's storm-page-in wrapper is the reference implementation.

rules.name: The Bounded Layout-Animation Exception
rules.body: The sidebar's width transition is the one sanctioned exception to transform/opacity-only animation in .storm: it is the literal collapsible-sidebar feature, scoped to one fixed-position element, user-triggered only, mitigated with will-change and disabled under reduced motion. Not precedent for animating layout properties elsewhere.

rules.name: The One System, Two Planes Rule
rules.body: Dark mode is the same Tailwind colour-key names resolving to different CSS-variable values, never a per-component dark: variant. New admin components must use the Tailwind colour keys, not literal hex values or dark: prefixes.

dos: Do keep every admin style inside the .storm scope (rooted at #storm-root), and re-check any new global h1..h4 rule in globals.css against the storm heading reclaim.
Do reach for the Tailwind colour keys (bg-paper-lift, text-rain, border-mist, bg-elevated, bg-scrim, ...) for anything that must repaint correctly in dark mode.
Do use scrim (never ink) for overlays, and accent (never ink) for fixed-colour brand chips.
Do carry status with the four-family soft-fill pill system, applied identically to pills, badges, KPI numbers and toasts, in both themes.
Do give every rounded surface a shadow token (storm-xs at minimum) — nothing in this world sits flat.
Do strip a persistent wrapper's fill-mode animation class on onAnimationEnd if it uses both/forwards on a transform-based keyframe.
Do use tabular numerals on every count, price and date so columns align.
Do give every roster a designed sub-lg record-card list rather than letting a table scroll sideways.
Do put sticky positioning and borders on individual th elements, not thead, for any sticky table header.
donts: Don't reintroduce the discarded ledger system's vocabulary into .storm: no zero-radius overrides, no letter-spaced caps kickers or eyebrows outside the existing sidebar group-label exception, no ink-weight-only status, no giant uppercase monument word.
Don't let a hue outside a status pill's assigned family stand in for that status.
Don't animate a status pill on mount — the cross-fade belongs to an actual state change, not to page load.
Don't carry customer-world material (glow shadows, frosted glass, cyan, Manrope) into the admin world, or Framer Product Console material into the customer world.
Don't make whole-row click the only path to a record; the row link stays the keyboard and screen-reader target.
Don't animate width/height/top/left in .storm outside the one sanctioned, bounded sidebar exception — everything else is transform/opacity.
Don't regress quiet's dark-mode value below #8B8B8B; it was set there to clear WCAG AA contrast and carries real text.
